name: extractPageContent
description:
Fetches a web page and extracts its main readable content + outbound links. Uses the host-injected fetch (SSRF-defended in `strict` mode) and safety.parser.html for parsing.

Returns JSON: { title, content (with [n] link markers), links: [{index, text, url, linkTitle}] }.

params.name: pageUrl
params.description: Page URL to fetch and clean

humanInTheLoop.promptTemplate: The assistant wants to fetch and read a web page. Allow '{toolName}' with {args}?

name: getCurrentTime
description: Returns the current time in ISO 8601 format. If the user specifies a city, country, or location, the agent should first map it to an IANA time zone and supply it via the timeZone parameter. If no time zone is provided, UTC is used.

name: getWeather
description: Free public weather lookup via wttr.in (no API key). Returns a small JSON summary: { location, tempC, humidity, windSpeed, windDirection }.

params.name: location
params.description: City / region name (e.g. 'Seoul', 'New York'). Empty = caller's IP-detected location.

name: googlePseSearch
description:
Google Programmable Search Engine query (Custom Search API). Requires `GOOGLE_API_KEY` and `GOOGLE_PSE_ID` env vars.

Setup:
 1. Create / open a project at console.cloud.google.com, enable 'Custom Search API', issue an API key.
 2. Create a Programmable Search Engine at programmablesearchengine.google.com and copy its ID.
 3. Export the values:  GOOGLE_API_KEY=AIza...   GOOGLE_PSE_ID=01234...

params.name: resultNum
params.description: Number of results to return (1-10, default 3)

name: openaiResponseGenerator
description:
Calls OpenAI's Responses API. Requires `OPENAI_API_KEY` env var.

Setup:
 1. Sign in at platform.openai.com and issue an API key.
 2. Export it:  OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-...

params.name: prompt
params.testValue: Summarise Spring AI in one paragraph.

humanInTheLoop.promptTemplate: The assistant wants to call the OpenAI API, which spends API credits. Allow '{toolName}' with {args}?

name: sendSlackMessage
description:
Posts a text message to a Slack channel via Incoming Webhook. Requires `SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL` env var (the full https://hooks.slack.com/services/... URL).

Setup:
 1. Create a Slack app at api.slack.com/apps, enable 'Incoming Webhooks'.
 2. Add a webhook to the target channel and copy the URL.
 3. Export it:  SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL=https://hooks.slack.com/services/...

humanInTheLoop.promptTemplate: The assistant wants to send a Slack message. Allow '{toolName}' with {args}?

name: sendEmail
description: Use this whenever the user wants to email or send something to someone — it is the only way you send email for the user. You do NOT send it yourself: calling this makes a "Send email" button appear in the chat, and the user clicks it to send from their own mail app (review-then-send). So always call this tool for email requests; never refuse with "I can't send email" and never write the email as plain text instead. IMPORTANT — after calling, the email is NOT sent yet: do NOT say it was sent (never "전송되었습니다" / "sent"). Instead tell the user to click the "Send email" button below to send it (e.g. "메일 초안을 준비했어요 — 아래 Send email 버튼을 눌러 보내세요"). The button appears automatically; you do not need to paste any code block. 'subject' and 'body' are required; 'to' and 'cc' are optional (comma-separated). The From/sender address cannot be set (it is the user's default account).

params.name: body
params.description: Email body text. Plain text; line breaks are kept.
params.testValue: Hi Alice, following up on our chat.

name: addToCalendar
description: Use this whenever the user wants to add a calendar event or schedule something — it is the only way you add events for the user. You do NOT add it yourself: calling this makes an "Add to calendar" button appear in the chat, and the user clicks it to download a standard .ics file that opens in their own calendar app (Apple Calendar, Outlook, Google import, etc.). So always call this tool for scheduling requests; never refuse and never write the event as plain text instead. IMPORTANT — after calling, the event is NOT added yet: do NOT say it was added/created. Instead tell the user to click the "Add to calendar" button below to add it (e.g. "일정을 준비했어요 — 아래 Add to calendar 버튼을 눌러 추가하세요"). The button appears automatically; you do not need to paste any code block. Convert rough date/time (e.g. 'tomorrow 10am') to ISO-8601 first; 'end' must be after 'start'. 'title', 'start', 'end' are required; 'location' and 'description' are optional.

params.name: start
params.description: Start time as ISO-8601 (convert rough input first, e.g. 2026-01-15T10:00:00+09:00).

params.name: end
params.description: End time as ISO-8601, after start.

name: showLocation
description: Use this when the user asks where a place is or wants to see a location. Calling this renders an interactive map centered on the place directly in the chat - you do NOT need to paste coordinates or a link. Pass a place name, address, or 'lat,lng' as 'query'. After calling, tell the user the location is shown on the map below (e.g. "아래 지도에 위치를 표시했어요"). The map is display-only and needs no account or key.

params.name: query
params.description: Place name, address, or 'lat,lng' to show on the map.

params.name: label
params.description: Optional short caption shown above the map.

name: plotPointsOnMap
description: Renders an interactive world map with MULTIPLE markers directly in the chat. Use this to plot several geographic points at once (e.g. earthquakes, cities, store locations). Pass 'points' as a JSON array; each item needs numeric 'lat' and 'lng', plus an optional 'label' and an optional numeric 'weight' (or 'mag') that sizes and colors the marker. After calling, tell the user the map is shown below. Display-only, no account or key. Optional 'style' picks the basemap (light or dark); default is light and the user can also toggle it on the map.

params.name: points
params.description: JSON array of points, each {lat, lng, label?, weight?}. Example: [{"lat":36.47,"lng":70.76,"label":"Afghanistan M6.1","weight":6.1}]

params.name: title
params.description: Optional short caption shown above the map.

name: renderChart
description: Renders a chart directly in the chat from data you provide: bar, line, area, pie, radar, scatter, or gauge. Use this to visualize numbers you have gathered. 'labels' is a JSON array of category names (x-axis categories, pie slice names, or radar axes). 'series' is EITHER a JSON array of numbers (single series) OR a JSON array of {"name":..., "data":[...]} objects (multiple series). Per type: bar/line/area use labels + numeric series; pie uses labels + one numeric series; radar uses labels as axes + one or more {name,data} series; scatter uses series of [x,y] number pairs (labels optional); gauge shows ONE number (pass series as [value], optional 'max'). Optional 'sort' ('asc' or 'desc'; single-series bar or pie only) reorders categories by value: use 'asc' for categories with no inherent order (countries, products) so bars grow small to large, and omit it for time or ordinal categories (years, months, stages). After calling, tell the user the chart is shown below.

params.name: chartType
params.description: One of: bar, line, area, pie, radar, scatter, gauge.

params.name: labels
params.description: JSON array of category labels (axes for radar). Optional for scatter/gauge. Example: ["Bitcoin","Ethereum","Solana"]

params.name: series
params.description: JSON array of numbers for one series, or array of {name,data} for several. For scatter use [[x,y],...]; for gauge use a single [value]. Example: [62000,2400,140]

params.name: max
params.description: Optional maximum value for the gauge chart (defaults to a sensible round number).

params.name: seriesName
params.description: Optional name for a single series, shown in the legend and tooltip.

params.name: sort
params.description: Optional category order for single-series bar/pie: 'asc' or 'desc'. Omit for time or ordinal categories.

name: renderDiagram
description: Renders a Mermaid diagram directly in the chat (flowchart, sequence, gantt, mindmap, pie, ER, state, timeline, and more). Use this to show a process, architecture, timeline, relationship, or org chart as a real diagram instead of plain text. Pass the Mermaid source as 'code', starting with the diagram type, e.g. 'flowchart LR', 'sequenceDiagram', 'gantt', 'mindmap', 'erDiagram', 'stateDiagram-v2', or 'timeline'. After calling, tell the user the diagram is shown below.

params.name: code
params.description:
Mermaid diagram source. Start with the diagram type. Example: flowchart LR
  A[Start] --> B{OK?}
  B -->|Yes| C[Ship]
  B -->|No| D[Fix]
params.testValue:
flowchart LR
  A[Start] --> B{OK?}
  B -->|Yes| C[Ship]
  B -->|No| D[Fix]

params.name: title
params.description: Optional title shown in bold above the diagram.

name: showImage
description: Displays an image from a public URL directly in the chat (a photo, a chart image, a diagram, or a QR code you have a link to). Provide a direct https image 'url' and an optional 'caption'. Use only direct image URLs (typically ending in .png/.jpg/.jpeg/.gif/.webp/.svg). After calling, tell the user the image is shown below.

params.name: url
params.description: Direct https URL of the image to display.

params.name: caption
params.description: Optional caption shown as the card title and below the image.

name: renderDiff
description: Compares two texts (or two files you have read) line by line and shows a side-by-side diff card: lines only on the left are red, lines only on the right are green. If the two are almost entirely different it shows a 'completely different' banner. Pass the two texts as 'left' and 'right' with optional 'leftLabel'/'rightLabel' (e.g. file names). To compare files, read them first with readTextFile and pass the contents.

params.name: leftLabel
params.description: Optional label for the left side (e.g. file name).

params.name: rightLabel
params.description: Optional label for the right side.

name: renderTable
description: Renders a sortable, searchable data table in the chat. Pass 'columns' as a JSON array of {key, label, align?('right'), format?('number'), heat?(true to shade the cell by value)} and 'rows' as a JSON array of objects keyed by each column key. Optional 'sortable' and 'searchable' ('true'/'false'). Good for any list of records (prices, issues, search results).

params.name: rows
params.description: JSON array of row objects keyed by column key.

params.name: searchable
params.description: Optional 'true' to enable a filter box.

name: renderStatCards
description: Renders a row of KPI / metric tiles in the chat. Pass 'cards' as a JSON array of {label, value, delta?, trend?('up'|'down'|'flat')}. Use for headline numbers like prices, counts, or weather readings.

params.name: cards
params.description: JSON array of {label, value, delta?, trend?}.

name: renderComparison
description: Renders a side-by-side comparison table for two or more entities. 'entities' is a JSON array of names (the columns). 'rows' is a JSON array of {label, values:[...], best?(0-based index of the winning value, optional)}.

name: renderTimeline
description: Renders a vertical event timeline in the chat. 'events' is a JSON array of {date, title, detail?}. Use for histories, schedules, or sequences of dated events.

name: renderCandlestick
description: Renders an OHLC candlestick chart in the chat. 'data' is a JSON array of {t (label or date), o, h, l, c, v?} objects (open/high/low/close, optional volume). Set 'volume' to 'true' to overlay trading volume. Pairs with crypto or stock candle tools.

params.name: data
params.description: JSON array of {t, o, h, l, c, v?} candles, open/high/low/close (t may also be given as date or time).

name: renderHeatmap
description: Renders a 2D heatmap in the chat. 'xLabels' and 'yLabels' are JSON arrays of category names. 'data' is a JSON array of [xIndex, yIndex, value] triples. Good for activity-by-day-and-hour, correlation, or any matrix of numbers.

params.name: xLabels
params.description: JSON array of x-axis category names.

params.name: yLabels
params.description: JSON array of y-axis category names.

params.name: data
params.description: JSON array of [xIndex, yIndex, value] triples (objects {x, y, value} are also accepted).

name: renderSankey
description: Renders a Sankey flow diagram in the chat. 'nodes' is a JSON array of node names (or {name} objects). 'links' is a JSON array of {source, target, value} where source/target are node names.

name: renderFunnel
description: Renders a funnel chart for staged, descending values in the chat. 'data' is a JSON array of {name, value} objects, usually ordered from largest to smallest stage.

name: renderTreemap
description: Renders a treemap of hierarchical part-of-whole data in the chat. 'data' is a JSON array of {name, value, children?:[...]} nodes; nested children are allowed for hierarchy.

name: renderGraph
description: Renders a network/relationship graph in the chat using a force-directed layout. 'nodes' is a JSON array of node names (or {name, value?, category?, symbolSize?} objects; value scales node size, category groups and colors them). 'links' is a JSON array of {source, target, value?} where source/target are node names. Set 'directed' to true for arrowed edges. Good for dependencies, social graphs, knowledge maps.

params.name: nodes
params.description: JSON array of node names or {name, value?, category?, symbolSize?} objects (value scales node size, or pass symbolSize for an explicit pixel diameter).

params.name: directed
params.description: Set to true for directed (arrowed) edges.

name: renderWindRose
description: Renders a rose (polar bar) chart in the chat, showing magnitude by category around a circle. 'directions' is a JSON array of direction or category labels arranged around the circle. 'series' is a JSON array of numbers, or [{name,data}] objects for stacked bands. A single series is drawn with one color per slice and sorted ascending by default (nightingale style) so slices grow around the circle; labels with an inherent order (compass points, hours, months, weekdays) keep their given order instead. Optional 'sort' overrides this: 'asc', 'desc', or 'none' to keep the given order. Good for wind direction, time-of-day distributions, or ranked category comparisons.

params.name: series
params.description: JSON array of numbers, or [{name,data}] for stacked bands.

params.name: seriesName
params.description: Optional name for a single series, shown in the legend and tooltip.

params.name: sort
params.description: Optional slice order: 'asc' (default for a single series with nominal labels), 'desc', or 'none' to keep the given order.

name: renderChoropleth
description: Renders a choropleth (region-shaded) map in the chat from a caller-supplied GeoJSON. 'geoJson' is a GeoJSON FeatureCollection whose features each carry a name property. 'values' is a JSON array of {name, value} keyed by that feature name; regions are shaded by value. Use 'nameProperty' if the feature name lives under a key other than 'name'. Good for per-region statistics.

params.name: values
params.description: JSON array of {name,value} keyed by feature name.

params.name: nameProperty
params.description: Feature property holding the region name (default 'name').

name: renderGeoHeat
description: Renders a geographic density heatmap in the chat over a real basemap (Light/Dark toggle). 'points' is a JSON array of {lat, lng, intensity?} objects; denser or higher-intensity areas glow warmer. 'radius' (optional pixels) controls the blur spread. Good for incident density, sightings, or any lat/lng hotspot map. Optional 'style' picks the basemap (light or dark); default is light and the user can also toggle it on the map.

name: requestFileUpload
description: Ask the user to upload a file from their computer (CSV, Excel, image, PDF, or any document). Opens an upload dialog in the chat; the chosen file is saved into this conversation's workspace and the tool returns its path (for example uploads/sales.csv). Excel files (.xlsx/.xls) are converted to CSV automatically. After it returns, read the file with readTextFile, and for tabular data pass that text to parseCsv. Use this whenever you need data or a document the user has not already pasted into the chat.

params.name: prompt
params.description: Short message shown to the user explaining which file to upload.
params.testValue: Upload the CSV or Excel file you want analyzed.

params.name: accept
params.description: Optional accepted file types as a comma-separated list of extensions or MIME types (for example ".csv,.xlsx" or "image/*"). Leave empty to accept any file.

name: describeImage
description: Analyze or describe an image the user shared in this conversation. Call this when the user asks about an image (for example "what is in this photo", "describe the image I sent", or refers back to an earlier image). If ref is omitted and exactly one image exists it is used automatically; if several exist the user is asked which one; if none exist an upload dialog opens. The image and its metadata are attached to the conversation so a vision-capable model can see it.

params.name: ref
params.description: Optional identifier of the image to analyze (its hash or file name shown earlier). Leave empty to use the only image or to let the user choose.

params.name: question
params.description: Optional specific question about the image.
